messages:
alex: Heads-up — ACME reported unexpected token surge on yesterday's invoice, ~+18% vs dashboard. They say their client retried a few uploads after timeouts. Can we triage?
maria: Oof. Do we have request ids or example timestamps?
alex: Customer provided one request id: rid-acme-9f8b. They say original req at 2026-03-15T18:22:10Z, client retried at 18:22:20 and 18:22:45.
tony: I'll pull gateway logs for that rid. Quick Q: are retries deduped by idempotency key or request-id?
jing: Our metering currently uses the final accepted write path tokens tally. Gateway may replay streams when TCP resets occur; if the backend accepted partial stream then the replay can cause duplicates. We dedupe by idempotency-key when present, otherwise we mark per-request id.
alex: ACME said they don't set Idempotency-Key in their SDK. Client is mobile, flaky network.
maria: If they didn't set idempotency-key we'd likely count multiple accepts as separate usage. Need to confirm if both accepts produced ledger entries.
tony: Pulled logs: gateway shows three entries for rid-acme-9f8b: accept at 18:22:11 (200), connection reset at 18:22:12, replay accepted at 18:22:21 (200) and then another accept after partial stream at 18:22:46 (200).
jing: Matching to metering: I see three metering writes with tokens 412, 412, 412 around those timestamps. Ledger writes matching -> that explains the +18%.
maria: That's consistent. Customer invoice = sum(ledger) so they were charged 3x. We should offer refund.
alex: Repro attempt: I mocked a minimal client with no Idempotency-Key and simulated conn reset after body sent. Steps:
```bash
# send payload then kill socket to simulate reset
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' --output /dev/null --max-time 1 || true
# immediately retry same call without idempotency header
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
```
Result: Backend shows two accepts and metering increments twice.
maria: Can we patch metering to detect quick successive identical token writes from same client/req path? Risky to dedupe blindly.
ton'y: (typo) tony: We should be careful — legitimate retries for different payloads could look similar. Better plan: add a short-term replay detection window at gateway that looks for same client (api key) + same content hash + small time window (e.g., 60s) and only forward if not already accepted. If idempotency-key present, use that authoritative.
jing: Implementation notes: gateway can compute a lightweight sha1(content+api_key) and set an ephemeral dedupe key in redis with TTL 2m when an accept is proxied to backend. If a replay arrives and the key exists, acknowledge with the previous response (or return 409 with guidance) but avoid duplicate backend execution and metering. Need to design what response we send so SDKs can handle it.
maria: For existing in-flight incidents, we need a refunds playbook. I'll create a ticket but we should capture impacted invoices by searching ledger for contiguous identical token writes with same api key and similar timestamps.
alex: I pulled ledger slice for that key: three writes at 18:22:11, 18:22:21, 18:22:46 all with same session id header and identical token_count=412.
maria: I'll queue a manual refund for ACME and mark as "retry duplication" reason.
ton'y: tony: Short term mitigation: update SDK docs and add example to set Idempotency-Key on retrying uploads. Also bump default SDK to set idempotency automatically for non-streaming calls.
jing: Also: add observability alert rule — when a single api_key has >2 identical token write entries within 120s, create an SLO violation alert into #eng-sre.
billing-bot: Invoice 2026-03-16-ACME flagged: refund requested by maria. Status: pending.
alex: Action items: 1) tony implement SDK idempotency default 2) jing implement gateway dedupe (redis key + 2m TTL) 3) maria issue refund + customer comms 4) alex confirm repro and retention of logs.
maria: I'll draft refund email to ACME: apology, explanation, and steps we are taking.
ton'y: tony: Short term mitigation: update SDK docs and add example to set Idempotency-Key on retrying uploads. Also bump default SDK to set idempotency automatically for non-streaming calls.
jing: I'll open a small RFC for the gateway dedupe and include failure modes.
alex: Thanks team. ACME rep appreciated quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
